review.summary: El Tajín flourished approximately 800–1100 CE. Its urban and ceremonial buildings occupied a locally adapted landscape; this phase is not a founding date for every building.
review.limitations: The interval describes the cited archaeological phase; its end does not by itself establish abandonment. Later and earlier use may exist beyond this record. Official INAH public archaeological site point; not a complete urban boundary or footprint.
review.discussion: Known physical location and uncertainty about dates, functions and resident counts are separate questions. Descendant communities and cultural relationships continue beyond the archaeological phase.
review.provenance: Individually curated public heritage/archaeological sources; no confidential coordinates and no inferred building footprints.
history: Added an individual place to complement regional evidence.
